claim: In its FQ4-26 results (30 Sep 2026) Micron expects industry DRAM bit shipments to grow in the mid-20s percent in calendar 2026.
evidence: "In DRAM, for calendar 2026, we expect industry bit shipments to grow in the mid-20s percentage range." (Micron FQ4-26 deck, p. 16 'Market Outlook (1 of 2)')
notes: Updates the 'low- to mid-20s' outlook of 24 Jun 2026 (CLM-1331).

claim: In its FQ4-26 results (30 Sep 2026) Micron expects industry NAND bit shipments to grow in the low-20s percent in calendar 2026, slightly above its prior expectation.
evidence: "In NAND, for calendar 2026, we expect industry bit shipments to grow in the low-20s percentage range, slightly above our prior expectations." (Micron FQ4-26 deck, p. 16)

claim: Deloitte's own inputs imply that about 20 million gen-AI chips would be roughly 0.002% of the ~1.05 trillion chips sold annually, not the 'roughly 0.2%' its 2026 outlook states.
evidence: Endnote 7: "SIA estimates 1.05 trillion units of total chip sales for the full year 2025"; endnote 8: "the annual total number of AI chips produced could be about 20 million." 20e6 / 1.05e12 = 0.0019%.

metric.name: gen-AI chips share of unit volume (recomputed)
metric.period: CY2026 AI chips vs CY2025 total units
metric.population: generative-AI chips vs all chips sold
metric.methodology: division of the two figures in Deloitte endnotes 7 and 8

notes: Inference from SRC-0430 endnotes 7-8; contradicts the 0.2% value recorded in CLM-1325.
